gap: No result ChatGPT got puts measured always-on power draw side by side for the NAS candidates. PCWorld measured its pick, the QNAP TS-264, at 26.5 W idle. ComputerBase measured the UGREEN DXP2800 and Synology DS224+ at 18.6 W idle each. raspberry.tips measured that a running HAOS VM adds only about 1–2 W on a DXP2800.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages: QNAP FAQ (Virtualization Station USB passthrough), UGREEN KB 642 and 911, Synology VMM spec for DSM 7.4, and smarthomejunkie's DXP4800 GT guide. None of the readable ones gives a wattage. The smarthomejunkie page failed with a certificate error, so I couldn't check it. The uncited raspberry.tips UGREEN guide, at rank 5, has part of the finding: one DXP2800 measured with and without the HA VM. No result compares models, and none has the PCWorld, ComputerBase, KitGuru or NASCompares lab figures.
decides: This doesn't decide whether USB Zigbee passthrough works. It does work as a tiebreak on running cost for a box that's on 24/7. ChatGPT's top pick, the QNAP TS-264, drew 26.5 W idle in PCWorld's test, against 18.6 W for the DXP2800 and DS224+ in ComputerBase's test. That gap is about 69 kWh a year: 7.9 W × 8,760 h. The DS925+ (28 W, NASCompares) and the DXP4800 Plus (24.25 W, KitGuru) cost more to run than either 2-bay. The HA VM itself adds only about 1–2 W (raspberry.tips). The labs used different drives and setups, so these figures show the size of the gap, not exact differences.

findings.label: Whole-system power with Home Assistant OS VM running vs VM stopped
findings.value: 15–17 W with the HA VM active (idle); 14–15 W with the VM stopped and drives active; 8–9 W with drives hibernating; up to 22 W at boot
findings.source_title: Home Assistant on a UGREEN NAS – VM Guide | raspberry.tips
findings.note: raspberry.tips, article dated 2026-10-21. Measured with a smart power meter at the wall. Setup: two Seagate IronWolf drives in RAID 1, HAOS VM with 2 cores and 4 GB. The VM costs about 1–2 W. The author estimates 130–150 kWh a year. The author hadn't yet tested Zigbee passthrough.

findings.label: ComputerBase measured power: drives asleep / idle / writing
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP2800 im Test (ComputerBase, page 3: Lautstärke und Leistungsaufnahme)
findings.note: Frank Hüber, ComputerBase, 2024-07-01. Chart categories: 'HDDs im Ruhezustand / Leerlauf / Schreiben'. The test drives appear to be 2× Seagate IronWolf Pro 20 TB, but the chart doesn't name them for this measurement. 18.6 W × 8,760 h ≈ 163 kWh a year.

findings.product: Synology DS224+ (predecessor of the DS225+, same J4125 platform)
findings.label: ComputerBase measured power, same chart as the DXP2800: drives asleep / idle / writing
findings.value: 3.5 W (7.0 W without extended standby) / 18.6 W / 25.3 W
findings.note: Frank Hüber, ComputerBase, 2024-07-01. This is the DS224+, not the DS225+. ComputerBase says the DXP2800 and DS224+ are 'in etwa gleichauf' (roughly level) at idle and under load.

findings.label: PCWorld measured power: idle / sleep / load / off
findings.note: Ines Walke-Chomjakov, PCWorld, 2025-12-23. Setup: two Seagate IronWolf ST4000NE001 4 TB drives in RAID 1. 26.5 W × 8,760 h ≈ 232 kWh a year, about 69 kWh more than the DXP2800's 18.6 W idle (ComputerBase, different drives). The review doesn't test Virtualization Station.

findings.label: NASCompares measured power and noise
findings.value: about 28 W idle; 62–64 W peak; 36–37 dB(A) idle, 48–50 dB(A) under load
findings.source_title: Synology DS925+ NAS Review – Good News, Bad News | NAS Compares
findings.note: Rob Andrews, NASCompares, 2025-05-02. Idle: base apps installed, no access. Peak: all four bays filled, SSDs installed, CPU under strain, both 2.5GbE ports active. Drive models aren't named. 28 W × 8,760 h ≈ 245 kWh a year.

findings.label: KitGuru measured wall power: idle / peak read / peak write
findings.value: 24.25 W idle (2.5GbE), 30.45 W idle (10GbE); 52.07 W / 58.17 W peak reads; 61.35 W / 67.02 W peak writes (2.5GbE / 10GbE)
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800Plus 4-bay NAS Review (KitGuru, page 14)
findings.note: Simon Crisp, KitGuru, 2024-05-28. Drives: WD Red WD60EFRX. Peak power taken at the wall during CrystalDiskMark 8.0.4 runs. 24.25 W × 8,760 h ≈ 212 kWh a year.

findings.label: Power draw stated by the maker (Nabu Casa), not an independent measurement
findings.value: about 1.7 W idle, about 3 W under heavy load
findings.source_title: About Home Assistant Green | Nabu Casa support
findings.note: Maker's own figure, for comparison only. The page doesn't say how it was measured. That's about 15 kWh a year at 1.7 W, against 130–150 kWh for a DXP2800 running the HA VM (raspberry.tips).

unsourced: Independent idle measurement for the Synology DS225+. The readable parts of the NASCompares DS225+ review (read 2026-11-08) only repeat Synology's spec: 16.98 W access, 6.08 W hibernation, 19.6 dB(A). The '10 W idle' figure from a search snippet couldn't be opened, so I left it out.

Measured power for the UGREEN DXP4800 GT. Notebookcheck's review (Abhinav Fating, updated 2026-10-05) has no power or noise figures. The Neowin and Vortez GT reviews returned 403. ComputerBase's GT power section didn't come up in search.
TechPowerUp DXP4800 Plus power page and Igor's Lab DXP2800 power page: both returned 403, so their figures (including Igor's Lab's 5.6 W standby / 14.5 W transfer from a snippet) are left out.
An independent meter reading for the Home Assistant Green. I only found Nabu Casa's own 1.7 W / 3 W, plus one Matter Alpha review that doesn't give a method.

Any named lab or reviewer measurement of USB Zigbee passthrough reliability, such as reconnects after VM reboot or drop rate. I also found none of HAOS VM CPU or RAM use on any of these NAS models. The evidence is only owner reports and guides.
